---
title: "Clean: dating services"
---

In the CSV from [scrape_dating.qmd](scrape_dating.qmd), the registered-user count and the reporting year are both embedded in one string, like `"30,000,000 as of 2006[2]"`. The user count always has thousands separators, so matching a comma-grouped number pulls it out first; whatever's left over is where the year lives. The "Free" and "All features free" columns are full sentences; we keep the first word (Yes/No/Maybe) as a clean category and leave the original text in place.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: clean-dating
#| message: false
#| collapse: true
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)

dating_clean <- read_csv("data/dating_services.csv") |>
  mutate(
    users_raw = str_extract(registered_users, "\\d{1,3}(?:,\\d{3})+"),
    registered_users_n = as.numeric(str_remove_all(users_raw, ",")),
    users_year = as.integer(str_extract(str_remove(registered_users, fixed(users_raw)), "\\d{4}")),
    free_clean = str_extract(free, regex("^(Yes|No|Maybe)", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    all_features_free_clean = str_extract(all_features_free, regex("^(Yes|No|Maybe)", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) |>
  select(-users_raw) |>
  filter(!is.na(registered_users_n)) |>
  distinct(name, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: view-dating
#| collapse: true
write_csv(dating_clean, "data/dating_services_clean.csv")
dating_clean
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: clean-dating-py
import pandas as pd

dating = pd.read_csv("data/dating_services.csv")
users_raw = dating["registered_users"].str.extract(r"(\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+)")[0]
dating["registered_users_n"] = pd.to_numeric(users_raw.str.replace(",", ""))
leftover = pd.Series(
    [r.replace(u, "", 1) if pd.notna(u) else None for r, u in zip(dating["registered_users"], users_raw)],
    index=dating.index, dtype="object"
)
dating["users_year"] = pd.to_numeric(leftover.str.extract(r"(\d{4})")[0]).astype("Int64")
dating["free_clean"] = dating["free"].str.extract(r"^(Yes|No|Maybe)", flags=2)[0]
dating["all_features_free_clean"] = dating["all_features_free"].str.extract(r"^(Yes|No|Maybe)", flags=2)[0]

dating_clean = (
    dating.dropna(subset=["registered_users_n"])
    .drop_duplicates(subset="name")
)
dating_clean.to_csv("data/dating_services_clean.csv", index=False)
dating_clean.head()
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## stringr has a slight edge

Finding the year means removing each row's own user count from its text first. `str_remove()` is vectorized over the pattern, so one call handles every row. The `.str` methods in `pandas` take a single pattern for the whole column, so the Python version loops over the rows with `zip()`.
:::

See [viz_dating.qmd](viz_dating.qmd) for the chart built on this.
